summary: SameSite cookie attribute change after ingress upgrade breaks SSO sessions for private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 401/redirect-to-login immediately after SSO redirect completes. Issue started within an hour of our ingress controller (edge-proxy) upgrade (v2.8.1 -> v2.9.0) in customers private cluster.

Impact:
- Multiple end users are unable to complete SSO login to Redwood Console behind the customer's private deployment.
- Session creation appears to succeed on the identity provider side, but subsequent requests to the console return 401 and users are returned to IdP for re-auth.
- Affects all tenant admins and many user sessions intermittently.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) running Redwood Private 1.7.2
- Edge/ingress controller managed by customer (k8s) recently upgraded to v2.9.0 on 2026-03-12 08:15 UTC
- Region: us-west (customer region)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Initiate SSO login via SAML to the company's IdP (Okta) from console.redwood.private
2) Complete IdP authentication and return to Redwood with SAML assertion
3) Observe final redirect to console and intermittent failure with 401 or immediate redirect back to IdP

Observed behavior:
- SAML assertion is accepted (IdP logs show successful assertion).
- Support logs show session cookie being set in the response, but browser does not send the cookie on subsequent requests in some cases.
- When cookie is not sent, API returns 401 and user is redirected to IdP.

Expected behavior:
- Session cookie should be set and included in subsequent browser requests, preserving the logged-in session.

Relevant logs/snippets (redacted):
- Identity-proxy set-cookie header: session_id=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Domain=console.redwood.private
- Browser devtools (problematic flow): response sets SameSite=None was not present; subsequent request does not include cookie.
- Edge-proxy (v2.9.0) access log shows initial post-auth response 200, followed by GET to /api/me returning 401 with no cookie header.

Immediate workaround provided by Support:
- Customer rolled back ingress controller to v2.8.1 and reported immediate reduction in failures.
- Temporary mitigation: configure IdP-initiated login to include prompt=consent (not a reliable fix).

Attachments provided by customer:
- HAR files (redacted), ingress upgrade job logs, Okta SAML logs, screenshots of browser devtools
steps_to_reproduce: Initiate SSO login via SAML to console.redwood.private
Complete IdP authentication and return to Redwood with SAML assertion
Observe final redirect to console and intermittent 401 or redirect back to IdP
observed_behavior: SAML assertion accepted by Redwood but browser does not send session cookie on follow-up requests intermittently
Identity-proxy sets SameSite=Lax on Set-Cookie header in responses when ingress v2.9.0 is in path
Edge-proxy logs show 200 on POST SAML callback then 401 on subsequent /api/me without cookie
expected_behavior: Session cookie is set with attributes compatible with cross-site redirects from IdP and is included in subsequent requests
Users remain logged in after SSO redirect completes
investigation_notes: 03/12 10:05 UTC - Support confirmed timing correlation between ingress upgrade and spike in SSO failures
03/12 11:20 UTC - Reproduced locally in staging by deploying ingress v2.9.0; observed SameSite attribute being rewritten from None to Lax in the response path
Hypothesis A: ingress v2.9.0 adds or normalizes SameSite attribute on Set-Cookie headers when certain proxy annotations are present, causing the cookie to be blocked on the IdP->SP redirect flow
Hypothesis B: header sanitization in the chain (edge-proxy -> identity-proxy) strips SameSite=None or Secure attribute in cross-site flows in some browser/agent combinations
03/12 13:40 UTC - Confirmed rollback to v2.8.1 removes the behavior (customer verified)
03/12 15:10 UTC - Collected packet traces showing Set-Cookie header values at each hop (edge, identity-proxy). Edge shows SameSite=Lax after upgrade; identity-proxy initially sets None.
comments: Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-12: We're seeing about ~30% of logins immediately fail after SSO completes. We rolled back ingress and it seemed to get better. Please advise.
Support (Asha) - 2026-03-12: Thanks for the report. We're investigating a potential SameSite header rewrite in your ingress upgrade. Can you share ingress annotations and any header rewrite rules?
Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-12: Shared ingress values and the helm release notes for v2.9.0. No custom cookie rewrites were configured but they use the default proxy annotations.

SRE (Mateo) - 2026-03-12: Reproduced in staging with v2.9.0. Edge is rewriting SameSite=None to SameSite=Lax for cookies set during cross-site POST when strict-csp annotation is present. Opening INT-5021 for tracking with infra team.

Eng (Lena Chen) - 2026-03-13: Confirmed identity-proxy sets Set-Cookie with SameSite=None for SAML callback as expected. The rewrite happens at the edge when the response passes through header-normalizer middleware introduced in v2.9.0.
Support (Asha) - 2026-03-13: Notifying customer of root cause and recommended rollback (which they performed). Planning patch guidance for private deployments.
Customer (NimbleFin) - 2026-03-14: After rollback the problem is largely resolved. We're standing by for a permanent fix or a recommended ingress config.

Engineer (Mateo) - 2026-03-14: Patch identified - add explicit passthrough for Set-Cookie SameSite=None tokens or disable header-normalizer for cookie-related responses. Drafting advisory for private customers.
resolution_notes: Root cause: header-normalizer middleware in ingress v2.9.0 rewrites SameSite=None to SameSite=Lax for cookies on cross-site POST/redirect responses when the strict-csp annotation is present. This prevents browsers from including the session cookie on IdP->SP redirects, causing apparent authentication failures.
Immediate action: customer rolled back ingress to v2.8.1 which restored previous behavior.

Permanent fix path: coordinate with ingress vendor/maintainers to add an explicit opt-out for SameSite normalization or update middleware to honor Set-Cookie attributes on upstream responses for known SSO callback endpoints. Alternatively, document a recommended ingress annotation to disable header-normalizer for private deployments using SSO.

Follow-ups: create KB article for private customers (owner: Mateo Ruiz), add an automated check in Redwood Private deployer to warn when ingress v2.9.0+ is detected and SSO endpoints are present (owner: Platform), link to INT-5021 for infra work.
Status: customer verified rollback success; patch advisory being drafted and expected to ship to customers 2026-03-20 after upstream coordination.
